from itertools import combinations

n = 17
target_edges = 28

# Try building a bipartite graph (automatically no odd cycles)
# Part A: vertices 0..7, Part B: vertices 8..16
# No 4-cycles means: for any two vertices in A, they share at most 1 neighbor in B

def check_no_4cycle_bipartite(edges, part_a, part_b):
    """Check no 4-cycles in bipartite graph"""
    adj_a = {v: set() for v in part_a}
    adj_b = {v: set() for v in part_b}
    for u, v in edges:
        if u in part_a:
            adj_a[u].add(v)
            adj_b[v].add(u)
        else:
            adj_a[v].add(u)
            adj_b[u].add(v)
    
    # Check: any two vertices in A share at most 1 neighbor in B
    for u1, u2 in combinations(part_a, 2):
        common = adj_a[u1] & adj_a[u2]
        if len(common) >= 2:
            return False
    
    # Check: any two vertices in B share at most 1 neighbor in A
    for v1, v2 in combinations(part_b, 2):
        common = adj_b[v1] & adj_b[v2]
        if len(common) >= 2:
            return False
    
    return True

# Try to maximize edges in bipartite graph with no 4-cycles
# This is equivalent to a (0,1)-matrix with no 2x2 all-1 submatrix

# Greedy approach
import random

best_edges = []
for attempt in range(50000):
    part_a = set(range(8))
    part_b = set(range(8, 17))
    
    edges = []
    possible = [(i, j) for i in part_a for j in part_b]
    random.shuffle(possible)
    
    for e in possible:
        edges.append(e)
        if not check_no_4cycle_bipartite(edges, part_a, part_b):
            edges.pop()
    
    if len(edges) > len(best_edges):
        best_edges = edges[:]
        if len(best_edges) >= target_edges:
            break
